title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Panko-crusted chicken thighs over rice with a mild, sweet Japanese curry sauce built on a browned roux — the one sold in blocks, made from scratch.
notes: The sauce keeps for three days and improves. Fry the katsu fresh.

ingredients.name: curry powder
ingredients.note: a Japanese blend if you can find one

steps.text: Cook the onions in the neutral oil until soft and golden.
Add the carrot and potato and stir for a couple of minutes.
In a separate small pan, melt the butter, stir in the flour, and cook to a light brown roux. Take it off the heat and stir in the curry powder and garam masala.
steps.tip: This is what the curry blocks in a Japanese supermarket are — a spiced roux. Browning it is where the depth comes from.

steps.text: Whisk the roux into the vegetables, then add the stock, soy sauce, honey, and grated apple. Simmer until the potato is tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Season the chicken thighs, then dredge in flour, dip in egg, and press firmly into the panko.
Shallow-fry in 1 cm of oil until deep golden and cooked through, about four minutes a side. Drain on a rack.
steps.tip: A rack, not paper — paper steams the underside soft.

steps.text: Slice the katsu into strips, lay it over the rice, and ladle the curry sauce alongside with the fukujinzuke.
